clinician.trajectory_summary: A 13-year-old girl with unremarkable family history presented at 9 months of age with a left flank palpable mass. Ultrasound imaging revealed bilateral polycystic kidneys with large kidney size and multiple cysts, consistent with autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD/PKD1-related phenotype). Kidney function, blood pressure, and microalbuminuria remained normal at initial assessment. At age 10, she developed progressive cutaneous manifestations including facial erythema, angiofibromas with malar distribution, and hypopigmented macules on the upper body, arms, and legs, meeting diagnostic criteria for tuberous sclerosis complex (TSC2-related phenotype). Retrospectively, some skin lesions were noted to be present in the first years of age. At age 13, brain MRI revealed multiple corticosubcortical lesions with morphological characteristics compatible with cortical tubers and calcified subependymal nodules, confirming CNS involvement of TSC. Echocardiography and ophthalmologic evaluation at age 13 were normal. The combination of early-onset bilateral polycystic kidneys (PKD1 phenotype) with progressive tuberous sclerosis manifestations (TSC2 phenotype) in a single patient with negative family history for kidney and hepatic cysts is pathognomonic for TSC2/PKD1 contiguous gene deletion. Genetic testing confirmed this diagnosis.
